chosen.premise: Dodrio evolves from Doduo when one of Doduo’s two heads splits into two, creating a three-headed species.
chosen.hook: Dodrio’s evolution is not a new head—it is one head splitting.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate Doduo’s two-head silhouette as one head divides, then label the level-31 evolution into Dodrio.
chosen.note: A highly concrete evolutionary contradiction: Dodrio is formed when one of Doduo's heads splits, not simply by adding another head. The transformation is easy to animate and supported by entries plus the evolution chain.

candidates.premise: Dodrio has three sets of hearts and lungs, which its Pokédex says let it run long distances without rest.
candidates.hook: Dodrio’s stamina comes from more than just having three heads.
candidates.visualIdea: Reveal three heart-and-lung icons inside Dodrio, then animate it running across a distance marker.
candidates.note: The three hearts and three lungs are unusually specific to Dodrio and directly explain its endurance. The premise could use the exact 'long distances without rest' wording for maximum precision.

candidates.premise: Dodrio’s three heads are said to represent joy, sadness, and anger—three emotions sharing one body.
candidates.hook: Dodrio’s heads may not just think differently; each one has an emotion.
candidates.visualIdea: Give each head a distinct joy, sadness, or anger expression, then show all three on one body.
candidates.note: The joy-sadness-anger assignment is concrete and visually expressive, but it comes from a single 'said to' entry and offers less mechanical payoff than the evolution angle.

candidates.premise: When Dodrio’s three heads face three different directions, the Pokédex says it is on guard and may peck.
candidates.hook: Three heads looking three ways is Dodrio’s warning signal.
candidates.visualIdea: Use three directional cones from Dodrio’s heads, then flash a danger warning as the cones separate.
candidates.note: A clear, filmable warning signal with strong textual support. It is compelling, but the general 'three heads scan in different directions' idea is slightly less surprising than the head-splitting evolution.

candidates.premise: Dodrio can let two heads sleep while the third stays awake, giving its three-brain body a permanent lookout.
candidates.hook: Dodrio never needs all three heads awake to keep watch.
candidates.visualIdea: Show two heads falling asleep while the third scans the horizon like a rotating lookout.
candidates.note: A distinctive sleep-and-surveillance mechanic, directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries. It is strong, though the permanent-lookout framing slightly overstates the source.

candidates.premise: Dodrio plans three times as wisely with its three brains, but overthinking can leave it completely immobilized.
candidates.hook: Dodrio’s three brains make it wiser—and can make it stop moving.
candidates.visualIdea: Stack three planning screens around Dodrio until the information overload freezes it in place.
candidates.note: The overthinking contradiction is interesting, but 'three times as wisely' is awkwardly phrased in the source and the premise turns it into a stronger causal claim than the entries clearly establish.
